title: Weekly chore rotation for three roommates
summary: Three jobs, three people, one Sunday reset — so nobody owns the trash forever.

blocks.title: Rotate three jobs, not personalities
blocks.body: Alex, Jordan, and Sam share a three-bedroom. The rotation below keeps kitchen, bathroom, and trash/floors moving each week so the same person is never stuck with the worst job twice in a row.

blocks.heading: This month's rotation
blocks.caption: Example names. Swap in your own; keep the cycle shape.

columns.name: Kitchen
columns.detail: Counters wiped, sink empty, dishes done or in the machine, fridge spot-check for science experiments.

columns.name: Bathrooms
columns.detail: Toilet, sink, mirror, and floor. Shared bathroom only — private baths stay with the person who uses them.

columns.name: Trash & floors
columns.detail: Take out kitchen and bathroom trash, replace bags, sweep or vacuum common areas once.

blocks.heading: House rules that keep it fair

items.label: Reset Sunday night
items.detail: New week starts Monday morning. If you travel, trade before you leave — do not leave a silent gap.

items.label: Trade openly, not secretly
items.detail: A text in the group chat counts. A sticky note left on a closed door does not.

items.label: Personal mess is personal
items.detail: Your bedroom and your dishes in the sink after midnight are not on the rotation.

blocks.title: When someone skips a week
blocks.body: They owe a make-up on their next free evening, not a lecture. Two skips in a row without a trade conversation means the group reopens the roster — silent freeloading is how rotations die.
